source.title: Machine learning and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns

hypothesis: A transparent blend of simple OHLCV-compatible predictors highlighted by the source—momentum, past market-adjusted alpha, and illiquidity—identifies a long-only top quintile of liquid perpetuals with persistent weekly net alpha. The long-only construction follows the paper's finding that crypto anomaly profits are concentrated in the long leg.
feature_definition: At each Monday open and for W prior completed UTC days: momentum=prior cumulative return; past_alpha_proxy=asset cumulative return minus contemporaneous equal-weight crypto-market cumulative return; illiquidity=mean(abs(daily return)/quote_volume). Within the eligible cross-section rank each feature to [0,1] and average the three ranks.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals with complete daily OHLCV. Each Monday require exact history and valid features, then retain top 50 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume. No future membership information is used.
portfolio: Long-only equal-weight top signal quintile, 1.0 gross, weekly rebalance.
execution: All feature inputs end Sunday. Enter at Monday 00:00 UTC open and hold to next Monday open. No same-bar close fill.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive top-minus-bottom spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 lookbacks positive after base costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 lookbacks positive; 2024 and 2025 each non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The paper fits machine-learning models over a much larger characteristic set and spot-market data. This preregistered adaptation intentionally avoids post-hoc model selection and uses only three source-highlighted predictors constructible causally from the available Binance perpetual OHLCV panel.
